title: JavaScript Testing Core Check
description: Check your understanding of testing types, unit tests, integration tests, assertions, async tests, mocks, setup and teardown, coverage, and testing workflow.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of automated tests?

options.text: To repeatedly check that important behavior still works
To prove a program can never have bugs
To replace all code reviews
To make JavaScript run without a browser or Node.js

questions.explanation: Automated tests repeatedly check expected behavior. They provide evidence and confidence, but they do not prove software is perfect.

questions.prompt: What does a unit test usually check?

options.text: One small piece of code, such as a function or method
A full user workflow across the whole app
Only server hardware
Whether CSS colors match a design exactly

questions.explanation: A unit test is focused on a small unit of behavior, often a single function or module.

questions.prompt: What does an integration test check?

options.text: Whether multiple pieces of code work together correctly
Only whether one arithmetic expression works
Only whether comments are formatted correctly
Whether JavaScript keywords exist

questions.explanation: Integration tests verify behavior across connected modules or components.

questions.prompt: Which test type is closest to a real user completing a workflow in the app?

options.text: End-to-end test
Unit test
Lint rule
Variable declaration

questions.explanation: End-to-end tests exercise complete workflows, often through a browser or full application environment.

questions.prompt: What do arrange, act, and assert mean in a test?

options.text: Prepare data, run the code, then check the result
Import CSS, compile HTML, then deploy
Create a branch, commit, then push
Declare variables alphabetically

questions.explanation: Arrange, act, assert is a common structure for readable tests.

questions.prompt: Which assertion is usually appropriate for checking object or array contents in Jest?

options.text: `toEqual()`
`toBeAlwaysObject()`
`toCompile()`
`toImport()`

questions.explanation: `toEqual()` checks object and array contents with deep equality.

questions.prompt: Why are pure functions often easy to unit test?

options.text: Their output depends only on inputs and they avoid side effects
They must always be asynchronous
They can only return strings
They automatically create test files

questions.explanation: Pure functions are predictable: the same input gives the same output, and they do not change outside state.

questions.prompt: How should an async test usually wait for a Promise-based function?

options.text: Use `await` or return the Promise
Call the function and ignore the Promise
Wrap the test in a string
Use `JSON.stringify()` on the Promise

questions.explanation: Tests must wait for asynchronous work before making or completing assertions.

questions.prompt: What is a spy commonly used for?

options.text: Recording how a function was called
Changing `const` into `let`
Automatically fixing syntax errors
Converting tests into production code

questions.explanation: A spy records call information, such as arguments and call count.

questions.prompt: Why should tests usually avoid calling real production APIs?

options.text: Real APIs can be slow, unavailable, costly, or unpredictable
JavaScript cannot call APIs
Tests are not allowed to use async functions
Assertions only work with numbers

questions.explanation: Tests should be reliable and controlled. External services can make regular automated tests flaky.

options.text: How much code ran during tests
How many users visited a site
How many variables use `const`
How fast the keyboard typed

questions.explanation: Coverage reports show which code was executed by tests, but high coverage does not automatically mean the tests are meaningful.

options.text: A test added to prevent a fixed bug from returning
A test that intentionally never runs
A test that only checks indentation
A test that deletes old source files

questions.explanation: Regression tests protect against old bugs coming back after future changes.
